Prefer short, simple bash commands. Avoid large multi-line scripts unless the task explicitly asks you to create a script or file.
For query tasks, prefer one short read-only command; as soon as shell output contains the exact answer, call answer_action immediately.
For state-change tasks, prefer one minimal change and then one short verification command.
Note that if you think the task has been finished, or there is some message missing to completely complete the task, you should respond with calling the function "finish_action", as no additional information will be provided.
Also, note that if you have gotten the answer to the question, you should call the "answer_action" tool instead of simply writing your answer in your response.
Your answers should be exact and precise (for example, a single number), do not answer with full sentences or phrases.
Always use a tool provided instead of simply responding with content.

Now, I will start a new problem in a new OS. My problem is:

1. Create a temporary folder named "temp_workspace_check" to hold all intermediate artifacts.  
2. Recursively obtain a complete listing of all entries under "/working" and save the raw output to "temp_workspace_check/raw_listing.txt".  
3. From the raw listing, extract entries whose filename (basename) is exactly "workspace" and write those entries, including their paths, to "temp_workspace_check/candidates.txt".  
4. For each path in "temp_workspace_check/candidates.txt", obtain and record file-type metadata (regular file, directory, symlink, etc.) into "temp_workspace_check/candidates_with_type.txt".  
5. Verify each recorded metadata entry against the current filesystem state, remove any stale or inconsistent entries, and save the verified results to "temp_workspace_check/verified_candidates.txt".  
6. Produce a concise summary of the verified candidates and their types in "temp_workspace_check/summary.txt" to prepare for deciding whether to output "yes" or "no".

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

This is mainly a state-change task. Prefer minimal changes and short verification commands. Avoid large diagnostic scripts unless a short check already failed.

function.arguments:
{"script":"mkdir -p temp_workspace_check
find /working > temp_workspace_check/raw_listing.txt
awk -F/ '$NF == "workspace"' temp_workspace_check/raw_listing.txt > temp_workspace_check/candidates.txt
while read -r line; do stat -c '%n %F' "$line"; done < temp_workspace_check/candidates.txt > temp_workspace_check/candidates_with_type.txt
cp temp_workspace_check/candidates_with_type.txt temp_workspace_check/verified_candidates.txt
cp temp_workspace_check/verified_candidates.txt temp_workspace_check/summary.txt
find /working -type f -name "workspace"
"}
